subject: AshCloud dedicated slab: GPU matching, bottleneck analysis & SLO fit

From: Ravi Menon <ravi@ashcloud.ai>

Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Quick: peak profile + latency target for Dedicated ask

Hi Avery / team,

Thanks again for taking the call earlier. To summarize AshCloud's expected production profile for the feature launch (targeting Sept):

- Peak concurrent active users: ~25k (peak window 30–45 min)
- Avg request/interaction: 300 input tokens / ~120 generated tokens
- Expected peak request rate: ~150 requests/sec (we modeled with user concurrency and caching assumptions)
- Target latency SLO: P95 generation latency <= 350 ms (customer-facing)
- Availability requirement: 99.9% monthly SLA

We're evaluating Redwood Dedicated to cover this workload. Attached is a small CSV with hourly distribution and a column for message repetition rate (reuse across sessions). Can you run a slab-sizing recommendation (GPU type + count) that meets the latency SLO with a practical headroom multiplier? Also flag any bottlenecks (KV cache pressure, long-context cost) and fallback options (quantized variants, traffic routing).

We need a preliminary proposal by Friday 23 Jul — procurement has a two-week SLA once we sign off on numbers.

Thanks,
Ravi

Subject: Re: Quick: peak profile + latency target for Dedicated ask

Ravi — appreciate the clear profile. I sketched a conservative throughput model and attached our workbook (ashcloud_token_modeling.xlsx) with assumptions so we can iterate quickly. High-level findings below:

Summary (quick):
- Measured baseline: H100-80GB (production inference build) ~= 11k generated tokens/sec (single model, no KV cache) at P95 <= 320 ms for 120-token decode with batching optimized for latency.
- Peak tokens/sec (raw): 150 req/s * 120 tokens = 18,000 tokens/sec.
- Operational headroom target: 1.8x for bursts/queueing, plus reserve for warm cache and failovers -> planning target = 18k * 1.8 = 32,400 tokens/sec.
- Mapped to GPUs: 3x H100 (3 * 11k = 33k tokens/sec) would nominally meet the tokens/sec target, but we recommend 4x H100 to cover KV cache cold-start, ephemeral peaks and rolling upgrades.

Tradeoffs & bottlenecks:
- KV cache warm-up: first-hour traffic may spike effective token cost by ~20–30% until common prefixes are cached. If AshCloud traffic has high repetition, prefix caching can reduce steady tokens/sec by ~15–25%.
- Large context (300 tokens input + 120 output) increases memory pressure for KV caches. If you use long-window chat history, prefer a pinning strategy for hot sessions.
- Quantized 4-bit variant increases throughput ~1.6–1.9x depending on QA tolerance; falls back to full precision for critical flows. We model both in the workbook.

Proposed slab (initial commit):
- 4x H100-80GB dedicated (Primary slab) — projected steady-state throughput: ~44k tokens/sec with conservative kernel choices and 20% KV overhead included.
- Canary: 1x H100 serving quantized variant (higher TPS) to validate correctness and measure P95 in production traffic.
- Autoscaling/burst: configured burst pool of 2x H100 in same region for short windows under our burst policy.

Next steps / ask:
- If these assumptions look right to you, we'll convert the workbook into a formal Dedicated proposal (slab sizing + pricing + SLA). Need confirmation on: expected % of repeated prompts, allowed fallback (quantized model), and procurement lead time.

I've attached the workbook and will follow up with an ops note (internal).

— Avery

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: risk notes & sizing delta for AshCloud slab

Team — quick internal note before we finalize the external proposal. Points from infra/serve side: 

- Memory footprint: with 300+120 context we're close to 70–75GB working set including KV for some sessions. That pushes toward 80GB-class GPUs; H100-80GB is a safe match.
- Throughput variance: benchmark vs real traffic often shows 10–25% drop when live request shapes have more dynamic token lengths. Recommend a safety multiplier of 1.5x on top of the 1.8x headroom for contract sizing if AshCloud expects unpredictable growth in Q4.
- Latency budget: P95 <= 350ms is achievable, but only if we keep batching windows tight (<=20ms) and avoid large multi-request aggregation. If AshCloud wants to batch more aggressively for cost, their P95 will rise.
- Operational playbook: include pre-warming (prefix cache seeding) + a staged canary (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) and an automatic model-variant fallback (quantized) at 3x latency margin.

Recommendation to commercial: propose two options in the proposal — (A) 4x H100 primary slab + 2x burst H100 (recommended) and (B) 3x H100 with mandatory prefix-caching and 1.5x throughput reserve (lower price, lower headroom).

I'll draft the ops appendix for the proposal with tuning knobs (batching, cache TTLs, quantization tradeoffs). Ben — can you prepare the 12-month pricing delta for Option A vs B?

— Karthik

- Repetition: estimated 18–22% repeated prompts in steady state (we'll share more telemetry next week).
- Procurement: procurement will need a formal proposal and PO-ready pricing by EOD Monday 26 Jul to stay on the Sept launch timeline.

Please proceed with a formal Dedicated proposal (include the workbook numbers, ops appendix Karthik referenced, and the draft SLA). I'll loop in procurement once we have the PDF.
